last_assistant_message:
## System Improvement Opportunities — Error Log Analysis

**Period:** 2026-07-21 to 2026-08-23 (since last analysis)
**Corrections logged:** 91 new (69 explicit, 17 self-detected, 5 unlabeled)
**Severity:** major/high: 22, moderate/medium: 49, minor/low/info: 18

Pattern log updated: `systems/error-tracking/patterns.json` now tracks 28 recurring patterns (was 19) — 10 existing patterns grew with new occurrences, 9 new patterns crossed the 3+ threshold. `_meta.json` `last_analyzed` moved to 2026-08-23.

### Top Recurring Pattern

**process-skip → protocol-skip** — 44 occurrences lifetime (11 new this period), pattern `pat-001`, still Tier 1/proposed and unresolved since March.

What keeps happening: agents (mostly Master) know a skill or gate exists — git, OmniFocus, master-slack, Plaud boot spawn, Cowork artifact registration — and bypass it anyway under time/execution pressure, usually rationalizing the skip ("no explicit request," "prior friction"). Four of the new occurrences alone are Master skipping the mandatory Plaud-ingest boot spawn.
Proposed fix: hard gate, not another rule — add a step-completion checklist to `workflows/boot/workflow.md` that blocks progression if `knox_spawn` isn't recorded in outputs, and equivalent pre-flight checks (skill-read attestation) in `client-meeting-prep`, `omnifocus-tasks`, and shutdown-cleanup git steps.
Fix type: workflow-update / rule.
**Recommendation: Needs your call.** This exact pattern has been proposed 3+ times before and never converted to an enforced gate — see "Systemic Note" below.

### Other Notable Patterns (new or grown this period)

| Pattern | Occurrences (new/lifetime) | Common thread | Fix type |
|---|---|---|---|
| missed-context → context-blindness (`pat-007`) | 4/12 | Master/Knox ignore context already available in the current workflow file or vault before asking David a question the source already answers | workflow-update |
| assumption-error → wrong-assumption (`pat-003`) | 4/23 | Guessing at ambiguous identity (speaker/attendee) instead of surfacing the ambiguity | rule |
| tool-misuse → tool-ignorance (`pat-004`) | 4/12 | Wrong tool chosen (raw bash instead of Desktop Commander/master-slack) for a task with a documented correct tool | rule |
| lazy-search → available-data-not-used (`pat-028`, new) | 3/3 | Master fails to cross-reference calendar data already pulled this session before asking David to ID a speaker, and accepts a subagent's negative result without a secondary check | rule |
| hallucination → wrong-assumption (`pat-023`, new) | 3/3 | Master fabricates specific facts (vault paths, speaker names, root cause) and relays them as established | rule |
| tool-misuse → protocol-skip (`pat-025`, new) | 3/3 | Agent bypasses the exact skill built to handle the failure it just hit (git, master-slack, rmapi), instead improvising or telling David to do it manually | rule |
| process-skip → wrong-assumption (`pat-027`, new) | 4/4 | Bias toward asking David a clarifying question instead of attempting the obvious next action first | rule |

### Agent Performance

| Agent | Corrections (period) | Top Issue |
|-------|------------|-----------|
| Master | 40 | process-skip (10) |
| Chase | 15 | process-skip (4) |
| Knox | 13 | process-skip / tool-misuse (3 each) |
| Jarvis | 8 | process-skip (3) |
| Harper | 7 | process-skip (3) |
| Chief | 5 | tool-misuse (2) |

### Trend

**Volume:** 2026-06: 89 → 2026-07: 126 → 2026-08 (23 days in): 53, on pace for ~69. That's a real drop from July's peak, but not yet two clean data points — treat as an early positive signal, not a confirmed trend.

**Resolution, not volume, is the real problem.** Across the full 350-entry log: 148 entries are still `proposed`, only 125 are `applied`. Fixes get drafted and logged but not converted into actual rule/skill/workflow changes at a higher rate than new errors accumulate. `pat-001` (process-skip/protocol-skip) has been proposed as a fix target since March and is still open at 44 occurrences — the single clearest case of a known, well-diagnosed problem not getting closed out.

**Compaction:** No months eligible — every month from March through August still has open (`proposed`/`in-progress`) entries blocking it, including 84 open entries sitting in July alone.

### Recommendation

The data doesn't need more analysis — it needs execution. Suggest treating `pat-001` and its Tier-1 siblings (`pat-004`, `pat-007`, `pat-025`) as a single work item: build the boot/workflow gates once, since they all share the same root cause (documented protocol exists, gets skipped under pressure, no hard stop catches it). That would also unblock July's compaction backlog.

**Minor housekeeping note:** `systems/error-tracking/error-log.json` (the legacy combined file, separate from `_meta.json` + `entries/*.json` which is what this analysis actually reads) is malformed JSON — looks like two structures concatenated without a comma around line 1725. It appears unused by `rebuild-log.py`, so it's not affecting analysis, but flagging it in case something else still reads it.

Files touched: `systems/error-tracking/patterns.json`, `systems/error-tracking/_meta.json`, `systems/eval-harness/skill-runs/rigby-error-analysis-latest.json`.
